questions.quote: Mimosa pudica (touch-me-not plant) closes on touching, whereas Helianthus annuus (sunflower) follows the path of the sun from dawn to dusk (from east to west).

en.q: Which plant closes its leaves on touching?
en.explanation: Mimosa pudica (touch-me-not) shows thigmonasty; sunflower follows the sun.

questions.quote: Table 19.1: Tropic movements - unidirectional, growth dependent, more or less permanent and irreversible, found in all plants, slow action. Nastic movements - non-directional, growth independent, temporary and reversible, found only in a few specialized plants, immediate action.

en.q: Which of the following is a feature of nastic movements?
en.explanation: Nastic movements are non-directional, immediate and found only in a few specialised plants.

questions.quote: Lenticular transpiration: Loss of water from plants as vapour through the lenticels. The lenticels are tiny openings that protrude from the barks in woody stems and twigs as well as in other plant organs.

options: bark of woody stems and twigs
